title: Cowork and Claude Code's 2026 Agentic Feature Push
content:
## Overview

Through the first half of 2026, Anthropic extended Claude Code's agentic architecture in two directions: deeper multi-agent orchestration within Claude Code itself, and a new product — **Cowork** — that brings the same architecture to non-coding knowledge work. This page covers both.

---

## Claude Cowork

Cowork applies Claude Code's agentic loop (read files, take actions, run for extended periods, report back) to general knowledge work, with **no terminal required**.

**How it's scoped:** Claude can only read and write files in folders the user has explicitly connected, and network access follows whatever egress settings are configured for the workspace — the same connect-a-folder model Claude Code uses for repos, applied to arbitrary documents.

**What it's used for:**
- Research synthesis — combining web searches, articles, papers, and notes into a coherent report
- Transcript analysis — extracting themes, key points, and action items from meeting transcripts
- Personal knowledge synthesis — finding patterns and connections across a user's own notes and research files

**Projects:** a Projects feature keeps files, instructions, and task context organized inside a single workspace, so a Cowork session doesn't need its context re-explained each time.

**Availability:** Cowork launched as a macOS/Windows Claude Desktop app for Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans in January 2026, then expanded to web and mobile for Max subscribers in July 2026 — following the same trajectory Claude Code took from CLI-only to web/desktop/mobile.

---

## Claude Code: Deeper Multi-Agent Orchestration

### Hierarchical (nested) subagent spawning

Subagents can now call the Agent tool themselves — a subagent can spawn its own children, which can spawn further children, down to a hard ceiling of **5 levels deep**. This enables layered task decomposition: a top-level coordinator delegates a module to a subagent, which further splits that module's files across its own subagents, without the top-level coordinator having to manage every leaf task directly.

### Background execution changes

By default, Claude Code agents still run in the **foreground** — the parent waits for each to finish before proceeding — but this became more configurable in 2026:
- Press **Ctrl+B** to background a task that's already running
- Set `background: true` in an agent's frontmatter to make it always run concurrently
- Setting the environment variable `CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT=1` makes *every* subagent spawn run in the background by default (this overrides any per-agent `background` frontmatter field)

**Caveat:** a backgrounded subagent auto-denies any tool call that would otherwise prompt for permission — a delegated file edit that would normally need approval silently fails while the subagent reports as if it succeeded. This is a sharp edge worth knowing before backgrounding agents that touch files outside an already-approved allowlist.

### Other Claude Code additions (H1 2026)

- **Claude Sonnet 5 became Claude Code's default model** (see the model history page for benchmarks)
- **Claude in Chrome** reached general availability
- **Claude Desktop on Linux** shipped in beta
- **`/voice`** — push-to-talk voice mode: hold spacebar to speak, release to send
- **`/radio`** — tunes into "Claude FM" (an ambient audio feature during long-running sessions)
- **Screen reader mode** — opt-in plain-text rendering via `claude --ax-screen-reader` or an environment variable, for accessibility
- **`CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER`** — lets Claude Code honor corporate launcher/wrapper configurations
- Vim users can remap `jj` to Escape and other insert-mode chord bindings

---

## Why This Matters

Cowork represents Anthropic explicitly extending the "agent that acts on your files over an extended session" pattern beyond software engineering — the same trust model (scoped folder access, extended autonomous execution, Projects for context) that made Claude Code useful for repos is now the template for general computer-based work. Meanwhile, hierarchical subagent spawning and configurable background execution make Claude Code itself capable of much larger fan-out — a single session can now decompose work across many more concurrent or nested agents than the original flat coordinator-to-subagent model allowed.
